info.title: delih
info.description:
Puts AI-generated code through an organization's own architectural rules, allows
      only small provable changes, and records every decision immutably.

commands.name: audit
commands.description:
read the chain: who did what, when
--limit <n>          default 20; the chain is verified
from the genesis row either way

commands.name: baseline
commands.description:
freeze today's violations as known debt.
WITHOUT --project it works store-less
like 'check', and says that no layer
debt is being frozen
--project <name>     use the index, and record the
baseline's hash in the audit chain
--rules <file>       same as check
--baseline <file>    write the known debt elsewhere
exit 1 = a new blocking violation

commands.name: bootstrap
commands.description: create the database and the owner/runtime roles (run once, as admin)

commands.name: check
commands.description:
apply rules.yml to a repository.
WITHOUT --project it needs no store,
no server and no scan: the syntax
rules (empty-catch, sync-over-async,
import) are answered per file. Layer
rules are then reported as NOT
MEASURED, never as clean, and no
audit record is kept
--project <name>     use the index: adds file-to-file
layer rules and the audit chain
--rules <file>       use a rules file from elsewhere
--changed-files <f>  narrow the SYNTAX rules to these paths
(a file of paths, or a comma list)
--dry-run            report, and never exit non-zero
--baseline <file>    read the known debt from elsewhere
--record all|none    a refusal is recorded in the audit
chain by default; 'all' records a pass
too (for CI), 'none' records nothing
rules <path> --project <name> --propose
write a starting rules file from what
this repository looks like. The layer
rules come out COMMENTED, each with
what adopting it would cost; the syntax
rules come out active
--out <file>         write it there instead of stdout. An
existing file is never overwritten

commands.name: churn
commands.description: how often a file changes, and with what

commands.name: create-project
commands.description: register a project to index into

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: verify the day-1 guarantees against the live database

commands.name: find
commands.description:
look a symbol up in the index
--limit <n>       default 50

commands.name: gate
commands.description:
judge a change BEFORE it is written:
the proposed content comes on stdin
--root <dir>         default: the working directory
--rules <file>       as check
--project <name>     also record a refusal in the chain
--require-analyzer   exit 2 when no analyzer reads the
file, instead of passing it
--json               one JSON object on stdout instead
of the text: status, findings and
each rule's 'remediation'. Every
outcome serializes, 'not-checked'
included - an empty violation list
is NOT a pass
exit 1 = refused. syntax rules only;
layer rules stay with check, in CI

commands.name: health
commands.description:
what the index can say without a model
semantic <path> --project <name> resolve references: dead code, cycles

commands.name: history
commands.description: read git history into the index

commands.name: init
commands.description:
wire the gate into a repository and PROVE it refuses:
writes tools/gate-hook.ps1, merges .claude/settings.json,
proposes rules.yml if there is none, then runs the hook it
just installed and insists on exit 2. Nothing is overwritten
--store <file.db>  also build the light index, so the
file-to-file layer rules work (~20 s)

commands.name: mcp
commands.description:
serve two ADVISORY tools over stdio,
for an agent to ask with before it
writes: rules_for_path and
check_proposed
--root <dir>         default: the working directory
Records nothing, blocks nothing, and
has no tool that suppresses a rule.
The gate is the hook; the enforcement
is check, in CI

commands.name: migrate
commands.description:
apply pending migrations as the schema owner
--test  apply them to the test database instead

commands.name: projects
commands.description: list the projects and their repositories, by name

commands.name: runs
commands.description:
what the recorded index runs say: status,
counts, and the NOTE in full - where the
reason a file could not be read lives
--limit <n>          default 10, newest first
the index's job record, NOT the chain

commands.name: scan
commands.description:
index a repository, skipping unchanged files
--force           re-extract every file: needed after this
tool is upgraded, since a file's hash
cannot see that the extractor changed

commands.name: status
commands.description:
where this repository stands, and the one command that
advances it. What bare 'delih' runs

commands.name: symbols
commands.description: list the definitions and line ranges in one C# file
